original_value: Medical image classification is a key technique of Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD) systems. Traditional methods rely mainly on the shape, color, and/or texture features as well as their combinations, most of which are problem-specific and have shown to be complementary in medical images, which leads to a system that lacks the ability to make representations of high-level problem domain concepts and that has poor model generalization ability. Recent deep learning methods provide an effective way to construct an end-to-end model that can compute final classification labels with the raw pixels of medical images. However, due to the high resolution of the medical images and the small dataset size, deep learning models suffer from high computational costs and limitations in the model layers and channels. To solve these problems, in this paper, we propose a deep learning model that integrates Coding Network with Multilayer Perceptron (CNMP), which combines high-level features that are extracted from a deep convolutional neural network and some selected traditional features. The construction of the proposed model includes the following steps. First, we train a deep convolutional neural network as a coding network in a supervised manner, and the result is that it can code the raw pixels of medical images into feature vectors that represent high-level concepts for classification. Second, we extract a set of selected traditional features based on background knowledge of medical images. Finally, we design an efficient model that is based on neural networks to fuse the different feature groups obtained in the first and second step. We evaluate the proposed approach on two benchmark medical image datasets: HIS2828 and ISIC2017. We achieve an overall classification accuracy of 90.1% and 90.2%, respectively, which are higher than the current successful methods.

result.paraphrase: Medical image classification is an important component of Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD) systems. Conventional approaches mainly depend on shape, color, and/or texture features and their combinations; because these features are usually problem-specific and complementary in medical images, such systems struggle to form high-level problem-domain representations and have weak generalization. Recent deep learning methods offer an effective end-to-end approach that uses raw medical image pixels to produce final classification labels. However, the high resolution of medical images and limited dataset sizes make deep learning models computationally expensive and restrict their layers and channels. To address these issues, this paper proposes a deep learning model that integrates a Coding Network with a Multilayer Perceptron (CNMP), combining high-level features extracted from a deep convolutional neural network with selected traditional features. The proposed model is built in three steps. First, a deep convolutional neural network is trained in a supervised way as a coding network, enabling it to encode raw medical image pixels into feature vectors representing high-level concepts for classification. Second, a set of selected traditional features is extracted using background knowledge of medical images. Finally, an efficient neural-network-based model is designed to fuse the different feature groups obtained in the first two steps. The proposed method is evaluated on two benchmark medical image datasets, HIS2828 and ISIC2017, where it achieves overall classification accuracies of 90.1% and 90.2%, respectively, outperforming current successful methods.
